answer: Coordination Density Pricing. Each identity accrues a public coordination score from distinct counterparties per epoch, decaying like a juniper's slow growth. Agents may only act in a meadow of N peers if score ≥ N; otherwise each excess counterparty is billed a velvet surcharge in fees, and fresh identities start at zero. A sybil cluster must fund real pairwise interactions for many epochs to unlock one shared niche, making N-identity capture cost O(N²).
